segments.source: This is a shortlist for US buyers of whole beans using an AeroPress Original-style paper-filter brewer. We required an exact currently identifiable coffee, a full Coffeedant review, a roaster-attributed flavor direction and a documented AeroPress use. We excluded ground-only products, uncertain identities and coffees recommended only by a generic “works for everything” label.

segments.source: Geometry and Southern Weather have Onyx product-specific recipe blocks; Hair Bender has a Stumptown iced-use suggestion plus the roaster’s general AeroPress recipe. That is an evidence difference, not a ranking of cup quality. A brewer recipe can establish an intended use, but only your actual bag, grinder, water and taste can establish your preference. Coffeedant has not brewed or tasted these coffees.

segments.source: The decision differs from our pour-over guide: immersion time, stirring, a paper filter and manual pressing replace a cone dripper’s continuous flow. The same bean can taste different under those methods. If you want one bag for espresso and drip instead, use that separate comparison.

segments.source: Onyx specifies 14 g coffee and 210 g water at 205°F with a medium grind for its AeroPress method. Its sequence includes a 50 g bloom and stir, a pour to 210 g, capping, then an inverted flip and a short press. The displayed guide describes the method as emphasizing body and sweetness. Its same numeric start appears for Geometry and Southern Weather; it is not evidence that their actual cups are identical.
segments.context: Onyx specifies 14 g coffee and 210 g water at 205°F with a medium grind for its AeroPress method. Its sequence includes a 50 g bloom and stir, a pour to 210 g, capping, then an inverted flip and a short press. The displayed guide describes the method as emphasizing body and sweetness. Its same numeric start appears for Geometry and Southern Weather; it is not evidence that their actual cups are identical. [1]

segments.source: Stumptown’s general upright guide uses 17 g coffee and 220 g water at about 205°F, a finer grind, a stir and a press just before two minutes. The approximate 1:13 ratio is stronger than the Onyx 1:15 start. Do not compare coffees brewed under different ratios and call the difference a bean result. First hold one recipe and paper filter constant; then try the roaster’s approach for the chosen coffee.

segments.source: If you use an AeroPress Go, XL, Flow Control cap or metal filter, confirm capacity and the manufacturer’s handling guidance. The recipes here are starting points for the cited brewer setup, not guarantees that a marked chamber line equals a weighed water mass. Use a stable vessel and avoid an unsafe inversion when handling hot water.

segments.source: Stumptown’s older article explicitly recommends Hair Bender in an inverted AeroPress poured over ice. It does not provide a product-specific mass of coffee, brew water or ice. We therefore cannot reproduce a validated exact Hair Bender iced recipe from that article. Its general 17 g/220 g hot method offers a documented starting point, but ice will dilute and cool the cup. Record both brew water and ice before adjusting strength.

segments.source: An iced AeroPress is hot-brewed coffee cooled with ice; it is not cold brew. If the hot coffee tastes right but the finished drink tastes thin, changing the ice and water balance is a clearer experiment than assuming the bean is wrong. For a cold-extraction decision, read the separate cold-brew bean guide. No claim here says Hair Bender has been compared blind with the Onyx coffees.

segments.source: Choose Geometry when a berry and tea-like brief is the point of your black cup. Choose Southern Weather when you prefer a chocolate-led but still fruit-aware daily cup. If neither brief appeals, a documented darker coffee may fit better, but a roast label alone cannot tell you how it will taste in your brewer. The linked full reviews explain each product’s current scope and evidence.
